l.i: 13 An opposita uni & eidem enti actu simul esse possint?

main_text.l: Probatur[?] negatiua. Rationes sunt: 1, Quia op-
posita definiuntur esse diuersa; quae uni & eidem enti
univoco secundum idem; ad idem & eodem tempore actu
simul inesse non possunt. 2, Quia opposita habent
inter se pugnantem naturam: Ergo ubi unum actu est,
ibi alterum consistere non potest. 3, Quia contradic-
toria non possunt simul uni & eidem inesse. Iam autem
omnia reliqua opposita tacite in se includunt contradic-
toria. Unum enim oppositum semper alterius oppositi
negationem in se continet: Ergo neque reliqua opposi-
ta uni & eidem simul inesse possunt: At in contrariam
partem obiici possunt haec argumenta: 1, Si opposita sunt

l.i: simul natura, sequitur illa etiam uni & eidem simul inesse posse:

page.notes: The Greek phrase in the first paragraph is too faint to read letter by letter and is marked illegible. The bold-looking opening word of the thesis paragraph ("Probatur") is a large decorative initial and is uncertain. The words "currutum" and "curruum" are not clear; the printed word may be "curvum" or a misprint. The left-margin labels (I., II., III., Obiectio., I., II., Responsio ad obiect., I., II.) are marginal notes that mark the argument's structure; their exact positions beside the lines are approximate. The signature at bottom right is partly cut off and reads as "D" followed by an unclear mark. Spelling of u/v and i/j normalised as instructed (e.g. Unde, uni, unum, Iam).
